    Theorem A from the data of Theorem 5.2 for minimal algebras #

    The assembly of Theorem 5.2. Lemma 3.1 reduces A to a split basic minimal representation-infinite algebra B (full corner, then a minimal quotient); Theorem 3.14 provides the data of Theorem 5.2 for B (proved here in the nondistributive case; the distributive case enters as the hypothesis DistributiveEmbeddingData); the functor Φ of Lemma 3.1 transports it to A, and Theorem 5.2 applies.

    DistributiveEmbeddingData is an intermediate hypothesis of the formalization. It follows from the data form of Bongartz's Theorem 6 together with Sections 3.3–3.4 and 4.2–4.5 of the manuscript (BongartzTheorem/Reduction/DataForm.lean), and the final proof in MainTheorems.lean removes it.

    source
    def LargeIndecomposable.DistributiveEmbeddingData :
    Prop

    Hypothesis: every distributive split basic minimal representation-infinite algebra over an algebraically closed field has the data of Theorem 5.2.
